This is NPR News Now. The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Windsor Johnston. The nationwide ground stop at paralyzed
airports across the country is raising concerns about the condition of the U.S. air traffic
control system. Departures were halted for more than four hours yesterday following problems with
radar and communications. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy says outdated equipment became
overloaded with data. He's calling for more funding to modernize the system, though Congress
has already approved billions for upgrades. Mary Schiavo is an aviation analyst and former
transportation department inspector general. This has happened before and most coincidentally,
or rather as in reading a crystal ball, the government accountability office on September 14,
2026 predicted exactly this. They said without some major change, the FAA will once again repeat
its history of cost overruns and missed deadlines. FlightAware.com now lists more than 3,600
cancellations today for flights within, into, or out of the United States. More than 1,800 flights
are delayed. President Trump is traveling to the Philippines and China next week. NPR's Deepa
Shiveram reports Trump will meet with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian leader Vladimir
Putin on the sidelines of the APEC summit in China. The White House says Trump wants to discuss
nuclear nonproliferation with Xi in Putin and the war in Iran, among other topics. The meeting with
all three leaders has drawn concern from Ukraine and European leaders that Putin could advance
priorities for Russia's war in Ukraine, which is nearing its fifth year. But a White House official
says Ukraine is not intended to come up in the meeting. Trump is also slated to have a one-on-one
meeting with Xi while in China. A meeting between Putin and Trump alone is not expected.
Deepa Shiveram, NPR News, the White House. An investigation is underway to determine why
a tanker collided with a docked cruise ship in New Orleans on Friday.
Eva Tesfai from member station WWNO reports more than 30 people were injured.
The American cruise line ship was docked for disembarking when the Atlantic asphalt container
crashed into it, knocking it on its side. 30 passengers and two harbor police officers were
taken to the hospital. There are no critical injuries and all other passengers have been
accounted for. Louisiana Governor Jeff Landry praised the response. We are going to get down
to the bottom of exactly what happened here and make sure that we make any adjustments necessary
so that the people that travel on the waterways here can know that they can do so in safety.
The Coast Guard is investigating the cause of the collision. For NPR News, I'm Eva Tesfai
in New Orleans. Microsoft says service is fully restored following a global outage.
It disrupted its software, including Outlook. This is NPR News.
Canada and the United States are making progress toward a trade deal.
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney says he spoke with President Trump and senior
officials ahead of a regional summit in the Philippines next week.
Canada is seeking to reduce its reliance on U.S. trade following the collapse of
negotiations in August. A parent's group is urging two state attorneys general to investigate
tech company OpenAI. NPR's Ritu Chanerji reports the company is accused of failing to protect
children. More than 60 parents of children harmed by tech platforms have signed the letter
to attorneys general Rob Bonta of California and Cathy Jennings of Delaware. Among those parents
are Maria and Matt Rain, parents of Adam Rain, a 16-year-old who died by suicide after prolonged
interactions with Chad GPT. Juliana Arnold is a founding member of the advocacy group Parents
Rise, which drafted the letter. They've been releasing products that are not safe. Kids have
died. People are being harmed. Arnold and others say they're asking the states to investigate
OpenAI's governance structure to learn what's preventing the company from prioritizing safety
over profits. Bonta is already probing recent cybersecurity incidents at OpenAI.
Ritu Chanerji, NPR News. An Asian version of the Eurovision song contest is making its debut today
in Bangkok, Thailand. Artists from 11 countries are competing, performing in 10 local languages
and English. The show is streaming free worldwide on Eurovision's official YouTube channel.
